about: A Zork-style underground adventure. A dream-wizard tells you to seek him when worthy. You gather things around the caves (bread, a staff), wake an old man in the Engravings Room, and open a secret door to stairs down that you are not yet ready to descend.

done.why: I got a staff from the cliff thief but never found where to use it. The Great Door's cracked rock stayed unmoved, and the grue passage needs a can I never found.

moments.note: Giving bread to the sleeping old man made a secret door appear.
The stairs refused me and said I was not yet worthy, which hinted at a longer quest.
The table teleported me into pitch dark without my lamp. I was returned safely.
Tying the chest to the rope and waiting while the thief opened it was a fun scene.
I could not work out what the staff or the cracked rock wanted.

wished: A clue about where to use the staff
Some way to find the grue-repelling can

lines.line: The way down is not yours today.
lines.why: It told me the quest needs more gathering elsewhere.

lines.line: The water has the look of a cold that would open your hands for you
lines.why: Strong prose that also taught the rules of the lake.

fun.why: The world has good set pieces, but I got stuck.

engagement.why: I had a clear goal until the staff puzzle stalled.

interestingness.why: The lake, the thief and the vista table are inventive.

prose.why: The prose is evocative, with helpful in-world hints.
